title: MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION
knowledge: Enumerates the 10 Rights in giving medication administration.
Discusses narcotics, high alert medications and LASA and its administration.
States the nurse's responsibilities with regards to safety precautions in caring for a patient who receives medicines that induces drowsiness.
skills: Patient's file is reviewed and the doctor's order is verified for medication administration.
Doctor's must use only the approved hospital abbreviation in prescribing drugs.
Pharmacy will dispense the right medicine as ordered and the nurse must double check the name, expiration date, color and consistency.
Medications are administered within the scheduled time, must be 30 minutes before and after the ordered time.

10 Rights of giving Medication Administration is observed: 1) Right patient 2) Right medication 3) Right dose 4) Right time 5) Right route 6) Right to refuse 7) Right Patient Education 8) Right Assessment 9) Right Evaluation 10) Right Documentation.
Written physicians order will be verified before medication administration.
The nurse who prepared the medication will be the one who will administer the medication and will be the one who will document in MAR sheet.
Clarification is done from the doctor whether oral medications can be given when NPO order is made.

Medications like anticoagulants, digitalis, insulin narcotics and other high alert medicines are checked prior to giving to the patient and must signed by two registered nurses after the administration.
Oral medication must be opened at bedside.
The nurse must remain with the patient until the drug is actually swallowed.
Safety precaution, no ambulation without assistance, side rails up and use of call light is instructed to patient who received narcotics or medicines that induces drowsiness.
Documentation of administered medication is done at the bedside.
Check for any side effects or adverse reaction to the administered medication.
attitude: Accept constrictive criticism as learning opportunity.
To be self-aware of limitation in knowledge and skills.
To be approachable and open to answer patients and family's questions.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.

Ability to organize and facilitate a Reflection session in and on practice after a Medication Administration learning opportunity occurs and activates findings to improve future practice and response.
